ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r10.claim: The first and final life both belong to God: human existence begins by His will, and the afterlife unfolds under His rule and law.
ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r10.anchor: zira âhiret ve ûlâ, sonu ve önü Allah’ındır. İlk vücûda geliş insanın kendi elinde olmayıp sırf Allah’ın hükm ü iradesine tâbi‘olduğu gibi sonu, âhireti de Allah’ın hükm ü kanunu dairesinde cereyan eder.

ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r11.claim: To attain one's final good, one must follow the proofs and rules God revealed rather than relying on personal wishes; bare idealism is insufficient without a sound practical basis.
ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r11.anchor: insan âhiretini kurtarmak, sonunda murâda erebilmek için sırf

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r22.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r22.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r22.claim: Both the afterlife and worldly life depend on God’s will, and intercession likewise cannot be considered independent of that will.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r22.anchor: gerek âhiretin gerekse dünyanın Allah’ın iradesine bağlı olduğuna, şefaat konusunun da bu iradeden bağımsız düşünülemeyeceğine dikkat çekilmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r23.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r23.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r23.claim: Tabari takes ‘the human’ in verse 24 to mean Muhammad, with these and the next verse indicating his high rank came by God’s grace rather than his own wish.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:19/r23.anchor: Taberî, 24. âyette geçen “insan” kelimesiyle Hz. Muhammed’in kastedildiği

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r2.claim: Idolaters follow conjecture and baseless wishes despite manifest guidance; desire cannot replace truth, and they will face the warned facts rather than what they wish for.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r2.anchor: conjectures and suppositions cannot take the place of truth, and false wishes and desires have no basis

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p50/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p50/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p50/r4.claim: Reward and punishment are realities, and conjecture or wishes cannot overcome them; all affairs of heaven and earth remain in God's hands.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p50/r4.anchor: Reward and punishment is a reality. They cannot combat reality with conjecture

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p54/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p54/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p54/r8.claim: The question about attaining desires expresses amazement at, and comments on, the preceding argument: wishes do not determine what reality grants.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p54/r8.anchor: This is an expression of amazement on what is said above as well as a comment on it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p55/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p55/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p55/r1.claim: When reality arrives, false hopes collapse: deities cannot help, and each person is judged by deeds, entering Paradise or Hell according to whether good or evil deeds prevail.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p55/r1.anchor: none of their deities will be able to help them in any way; each person will be faced with his deeds

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p55/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p55/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p55/r2.claim: The warning applies to everyone: Arabs, Jews, Christians, and Muslims also harbor desires invented by fancy; Islahi connects Jewish and Christian amāniyyu to al-Baqarah and Āl ʿImrān and says Muslims invented beliefs against Qur'an and Sunnah by following them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p55/r2.anchor: the Jews, Christians and Muslims too had a lot of desires in their hearts which were a product of their fancy.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p55/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p55/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p55/r3.claim: The Qur'an's general word “man” addresses every individual without exception: desires neither change reality nor make God's law biased.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p55/r3.anchor: By using the general word “man” in this verse, the Qur’ān has addressed each and every individual without any exception

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p55/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p55/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p55/r4.claim: Anyone expecting God's laws to accommodate personal wishes must know that both worlds belong to God; nobody can intercede or change His laws and decisions without His permission.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p55/r4.anchor: both this world and the next are in the complete control of God; no one has the status or stature to intercede before Him

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p18/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p18/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p18/r4.claim: God owns the afterlife and this world and gives or withholds from either as He wills; no one attains anything except by His will.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p18/r4.anchor: فلله الآخرة والأولى: أي هو مالكهما، فيعطي منهما ما يشاء، ويمنع من يشاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p18/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p18/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p18/r5.claim: The afterlife is placed before the present life because it comes later and to fit the verse ending, rather than following chronological order.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p18/r5.anchor: وقدم الآخرة على الأولى، لتأخرها في ذلك، ولكونها فاصلة

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:23-25/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:23-25/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:23-25/r8.claim: God alone owns the Hereafter and this world, giving from either to whomever He wills; no one can dictate to Him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:23-25/r8.anchor: { فلله الأخرة والأولى } يعطي منهما ما يشاء لمن يريد وليس لأحد أن يتحكم عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p111/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p111/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p111/r7.claim: Since God owns the afterlife and this world, He governs their inhabitants by His will, refuting the polytheists’ belief in idol intercession.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p111/r7.anchor: وفرع على الإنكار أن الله مالك الآخرة والأولى ، أي فهو يتصرف في أحوال أهلهما بحسب إرادته لا بحسب تمني الإنسان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p202/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p202/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p202/r6.claim: The Hereafter and this world are the two abodes, both wholly under God's ownership, power, and authority.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p202/r6.anchor: و: الآخرة والأولى الداران، أي له كل أمرهما ملكا ومقدورا وتحت سلطانه

JISHUMI:v9p6650/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6650/r1.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v9p6650/r1.claim: Abu Ali says God grants what benefits people: worldly and afterlife wishes, including religion, wealth, prophethood, and Paradise, but gives the afterlife to deserving believers rather than unbelievers; the author prefers this comprehensive view.
JISHUMI:v9p6650/r1.anchor: عن أبي علي، وهذا هو الوجه؛ لأنه يشتمل على جميع ما قيل فيه

JISHUMI:v9p6650/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6650/r2.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v9p6650/r2.claim: Another interpretation rejects the idea that a person may do whatever he wishes without recompense: God owns both lives, rewards obedience, and punishes disobedience.
JISHUMI:v9p6650/r2.anchor: وقيل: أم له ما تمنى، أن يفعل ما يشاء من غير جزاء، ليس كذلك

MUQATIL:53:23-25/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:53:23-25/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:53:23-25/r4.claim: During a public recitation of Surat al-Najm, Satan put a phrase praising the exalted cranes and hoped-for intercession on Muhammad's tongue; Meccan polytheists rejoiced and hoped for angelic intercession.
MUQATIL:53:23-25/r4.anchor: نعس فألقى الشيطان على لسانه تلك " الثالثة الأخرى تلك الغرانيق العلا " عندها الشفاعة ترتجى

MUQATIL:53:23-25/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:53:23-25/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:53:23-25/r5.claim: At the surah's end, Muhammad and the believers prostrated in affirmation of God, while Meccan polytheists prostrated at the idols; the elderly Walid ibn al-Mughira prostrated by lifting dirt to his forehead.
MUQATIL:53:23-25/r5.anchor: فلما بلغ أخرها سجد، وسجد المؤمنون تصديقا لله تعالى وسجد كفار مكة عند ذكر الآهلة

MUQATIL:53:23-25/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:53:23-25/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:53:23-25/r6.claim: After people hoped that angels would intercede, God declared that both the afterlife and this world belong to Him; the author links this to resurrection and recompense.
MUQATIL:53:23-25/r6.anchor: فلما رجوا أن الملائكة شفاعة، أنزل الله تعالى: { فلله الآخرة والأولى } [آية: 25] يعني الدنيا والآخرة

NAHHAS:v4p272/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p272/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p272/r6.claim: God gives whatever He wills to whomever He wills.

QURTUBI-FULL:53:23-25/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:23-25/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:23-25/r10.claim: God owns the first and later life and gives or withholds as He wills, regardless of anyone’s wishes.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:23-25/r10.anchor: فلله الآخرة والأولى } يعطي من يشاء ويمنع من يشاء لا ما تمنى أحد

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r14.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r14.claim: The second section reproaches Quraysh for idol worship, discusses its roots in ignorance and conjecture, and condemns seeking angels’ intercession.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r14.anchor: The second section (vv. 19–30) reproaches the Quraysh for worshipping idols

ASAD-NOTES:53:24/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:53:24/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:53:24/r2.claim: Both the life to come and the present life belong to God alone.
ASAD-NOTES:53:24/r2.anchor: despite the fact that [both] the life to come and this present [one] belong to God [alone]

ASAD-NOTES:53:24#n18/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:53:24#n18/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:53:24#n18/r1.claim: The particle means despite the fact that God is omnipotent and omniscient, needing no mediator between Himself and His creatures.
ASAD-NOTES:53:24#n18/r1.anchor: God is omnipotent and omniscient and does not, therefore, require any

ALUSI-FULL:v27p58#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p58#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p58#3/r1.claim: This explains the preceding denial: God alone owns all affairs of the afterlife and this world, so humans have no independent control; what God wills occurs, and what He does not will does not.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p58#3/r1.anchor: اختصاص ملك أمور الآخرة والأولى جميعابه تعالى مقتض لانتفاء

ALUSI-FULL:v27p58#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p58#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p58#3/r2.claim: The afterlife is mentioned first because rebutting the opponents' hope of winning there is especially important; the next verse follows from this point.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p58#3/r2.anchor: وقدمت الآخرة اهتماما برد ما هو أهم أطاعهم عندهممن الفوز فيها

BIQAI-FULL:v7p324/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p324/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p324/r1.claim: The quoted wish to receive good from God on return is denied: the speaker will not get what he wants, proving his subjection to the sole sovereign.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p324/r1.anchor: ولما كان الاستفهام إنكاريا , كان المعنى : ليس له ما تمنى , وكان ذلك دليلا قطعيا على أنه مربوب مقهور

BIQAI-FULL:v7p324/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p324/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p324/r2.claim: The whole dominion belongs to God alone.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p324/r2.anchor: وكان ذلك دليلا قطعيا على أنه مربوب مقهور ممن له الأمر كله

BIQAI-FULL:v7p324/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p324/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p324/r3.claim: The afterlife is where pleasures, fulfilled wishes, and their deprivation reach full realization; idolaters imagine their gods will intercede and make them prosper there.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p324/r3.anchor: دار اللذات وبلوغ جميع الأماني وحرمانها

BIQAI-FULL:v7p324/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p324/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p324/r4.claim: The afterlife is mentioned first because only those who follow guidance and resist desire attain their wishes there; nobody attains every wish in worldly life.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p324/r4.anchor: فهو لا يعطي الأماني فيها إلا لمن تبع هاده وخالف هواه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p324/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p324/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p324/r5.claim: The ordering is semantic, not for rhyme, since al-ukhrā would also have suited the rhyme.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p324/r5.anchor: فلهذا قدمها لا للفاصلة فإنه لو قيل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p112/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p112/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p112/r3.claim: The clause makes explicit the additional restriction implied by the prior verse; fronting for God expresses exclusivity, since the two lives belong to God, not people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p112/r3.anchor: وتفريع { فلله الآخرة والأولى } تصريح بمفهوم القصر الإضافي كما علمت آنفا . وتقديم المجرور لإفادة الحصر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p112/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p112/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p112/r4.claim: The afterlife and the first life mean the next world and this world, including all that each contains, as in the reference to the two easts and two wests.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p112/r4.anchor: و { الآخرة } العالم الأخروي ، و { الأولى } العالم الدنيوي . والمراد بهما ما يحتويان عليه من الأمور

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p112/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p112/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p112/r5.claim: The afterlife comes first to emphasize its importance and direct believers' concern toward it, while also fitting the verse ending.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p112/r5.anchor: وإنما قدمت الآخرة للاهتمام بها والتثنية إلى أنها التي يجب أن يكون اعتناء المؤمنين بها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p112/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p112/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p112/r6.claim: After denying that people control what they wish, the passage illustrates the point with the idolaters' hope that idols intercede, quoting their claims in 39:3 and 10:18.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p112/r6.anchor: ضرب لذلك مثالا من الأماني التي هي أعظم أماني المشركين وهي قولهم في الأصنام { ما نعبدهم إلا ليقربونا إلى الله زلفى }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p112/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p112/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p112/r7.claim: Even honored angels cannot intercede unless God permits it and wills to accept the plea for its recipient; idols, mere stones on earth, have still less claim.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p112/r7.anchor: الملائكة الذين لهم شرف المنزلة لأن الملائكة من سكان السماوات ( فهم لا يستطيعون إنكار أنهم أشرف من الأصنام ) لا يملكون الشفاعة إلا إذا أذن الله أن يشفع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p112/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p112/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p112/r8.claim: The move to intercession follows the denial that people get all they wish and underscores the gravity of intercession rather than abruptly changing topics.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p112/r8.anchor: فهذه مناسبة عطف هذه الجملة على جملة { أم للإنسان ما تمنى } ( النجم : 24 ) . وليس هذا الانتقال اقتضابا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p74#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p74#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p74#2/r1.claim: God alone owns the afterlife and this world; no one controls anything in either without His permission.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p74#2/r1.anchor: أي لا يملك فيهما أحد شيئا إلا بإذنه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p458#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p458#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p458#2/r1.claim: All affairs belong to God, who owns and governs this world and the next; what He wills happens and what He does not will cannot happen.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p458#2/r1.anchor: أي: إنما الأمر كله لله، مالك الدنيا والآخرة، والمتصرف في الدنيا والآخرة، فهو الذي ما شاء كان

BURSEVI:v9p194/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p194/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p194/r11.claim: God's exclusive ownership of both afterlife and present world explains why a person is not guaranteed the fulfillment of every wish.
BURSEVI:v9p194/r11.anchor: تعليل لانتقاء أن يكون للإنسان ما يتمناه حتما فإن اختصاص أمور الآخرة والأولى جميعا به

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p424#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p424#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p424#2/r6.claim: God owns both the hereafter and this world, giving or withholding from either as He wills; no one can dictate anything to Him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p424#2/r6.anchor: أي هو مالكهما ، فهو يعطي منهما من يشاء ويمنع من يشاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399/r5.claim: God is more powerful than creatures; were a child possible, He would be more entitled to sons than polytheists, though exalted above their claim.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399/r5.anchor: فلو جاز أن يكون له ولد - كما نسبه إليه المشركون

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399/r6.claim: God gives prophethood to His chosen one, not everyone who wishes for it, because He owns heaven and earth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399/r6.anchor: أنه لا يعطي النبوة من تمناها , وإنما يعطيها من اختاره لها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p190#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p190#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p190#2/r1.claim: God owns both worlds and rules over them, granting prophethood and intercession to whom He wills and approves, not to whoever merely wishes.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p190#2/r1.anchor: اى هو مالكهما وله الحكم فيهما يعطى النبوة وشافعة من شاء وارتضى لا من تمنى

RAZI-FULL:v28p261/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p261/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p261/r1.claim: One explanation: whoever chose a desired deity in worldly life will be punished here or, if not here, in the afterlife; 53:26 confirms that no intercession will avail.
RAZI-FULL:v28p261/r1.anchor: يعاقبه على فعله في الدنيا وإن لم يعاقبه في الدنيا فيعاقبه في الآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v28p261/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p261/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p261/r2.claim: Another explanation: since al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā rest on conjecture and desire, God's ownership shows idols have no authority; 53:26 answers the claim that they are angelic intercessors.
RAZI-FULL:v28p261/r2.anchor: هذه الأصنام ليس لها من الأمر شيء فكيف يجوز الإشراك

RAZI-FULL:v28p261/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p261/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p261/r3.claim: This may console the Prophet, who had explained his mission and God's unity without being believed: the deniers cannot escape God's power.
RAZI-FULL:v28p261/r3.anchor: هذه تسلية كأنه تعالى قال ذلك لنبيه حيث بين رسالته ووحدانية الله ولم يؤمنوا فقال لا تأس

RAZI-FULL:v28p261/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p261/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p261/r4.claim: It may be a conclusion from proof: after establishing Muhammad's revelation, including the message of divine unity, God's ownership of both lives confirms his truthful report of resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v28p261/r4.anchor: بقوله { إن هو إلا وحى يوحى } ( النجم : 4 ) إلى آخره وبين بعض ما جاء به محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v28p261/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p261/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p261/r5.claim: It may answer unbelievers who said believers were not better guided because they lacked worldly wealth: God gives wealth and guidance to whom He wills in either life.
RAZI-FULL:v28p261/r5.anchor: فقال تعالى : إن الله اختار لكم الدنيا وأعطاكم الأموال ولم يعط المؤمنين بعض ذلك الأمر

RAZI-FULL:v28p261#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p261#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p261#2/r1.claim: Al-ākhirah modifies either life or abode; al-ākhir is an active participle from an unattested verb, illustrated by أخرته فتأخر, though usage bars the expected form.
RAZI-FULL:v28p261#2/r1.anchor: صفة الحياة أو صفة الدار وهي اسم فاعل من فعل غير مستعمل

RAZI-FULL:v28p261#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p261#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p261#2/r2.claim: Al-ūlā is the feminine form فعلى, so its masculine أول is an أفعل adjective.
RAZI-FULL:v28p261#2/r2.anchor: المسألة الثالثة : { الاولى } فعلى للتأنيث ، فالأول إذن أفعل صفة

RAZI-FULL:v28p261#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p261#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p261#2/r3.claim: Every أفعل/فعلى pair requires a base; here, as with الآخر, that source form is unattested.
RAZI-FULL:v28p261#2/r3.anchor: كل فعلى وأفعل للتأنيث والتذكير له أصل فليؤخذ منه كالفضلى والأفضل

RAZI-FULL:v28p261#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p261#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p261#2/r4.claim: A past action is only truly past when complete; a hypothetical verb yielding آخر would mean reaching completed finality, although every completed action has an end after it.
RAZI-FULL:v28p261#2/r4.anchor: كل فعل مستعمل فله آخر ، وذلك لأن له ماضيا

RAZI-FULL:v28p261#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p261#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p261#2/r5.claim: The form تأخر is a reflexive or effortful claim to being last, not proof of a basic verb that makes someone truly آخر.
RAZI-FULL:v28p261#2/r5.anchor: وزن الفعل ينادي على صحة ما ذكرنا فإنه من باب التكلف والتكبر إذا استعمل في غير المتكبر

RAZI-FULL:v28p261#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p261#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p261#2/r6.claim: آخر is an active participle without a verb, intensified as أفعل; آخر is a connected part, while الآخر is separate and comes after it.
RAZI-FULL:v28p261#2/r6.anchor: الآخر فاعل ليس له فعل ، ومبالغته بأفعل

RAZI-FULL:v28p261#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p261#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p261#2/r7.claim: الأول has neither a verb nor a participle: an agent must precede an act, so the first cannot itself derive from an act that makes it first.
RAZI-FULL:v28p261#2/r7.anchor: فإذا الفاعل أولا ثم الفعل ، فإذا كان الفاعل أول الفعل

RAZI-FULL:v28p262/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p262/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p262/r1.claim: The apparent counterexample from سبق fails: سابق applied to the first is resemblance, since an agent and its act do not compete; تقدم was already answered through تأخر.
RAZI-FULL:v28p262/r1.anchor: الفاعل والفعل لا يتسابقان فالفاعل لا يسبقه

RAZI-FULL:v28p262/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p262/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p262/r2.claim: Rāzī rejects deriving أول from آل as “making another first” as far-fetched.
RAZI-FULL:v28p262/r2.anchor: وما يقال إن أول بمعنى جعل الآخر أولا لاستخراج معنى من الكلام فبعيد

RAZI-FULL:v28p262/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p262/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p262/r3.claim: أول and آخر are أفعل/فاعل forms, whereas قبل and بعد are neither forms; the words therefore differ morphologically even when their senses are related.
RAZI-FULL:v28p262/r3.anchor: فإن الآخر فاعل من غير فعل والأول أفعل من غير فاعل ولا فعل

RAZI-FULL:v28p262/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p262/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p262/r4.claim: آخر requires a specific afterness with nothing further after it; something can follow the first yet remain intermediate rather than last.
RAZI-FULL:v28p262/r4.anchor: ويؤيده أن الآخر لا يتحقق إلا ببعدية مخصوصة وهي التي لا بعدية بعدها

RAZI-FULL:v28p262/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p262/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p262/r5.claim: The relation is asymmetrical: arriving after everyone explains why someone is last, but being last does not explain every use of “after.”
RAZI-FULL:v28p262/r5.anchor: ولا تعكسه فتقول هذا آخر من جاء لأنه جاء بعد الكل ولا تقول هو جاء بعد الكل لأنه آخر من جاء

RAZI-FULL:v28p262/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p262/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v28p262/r6.claim: Rāzī cites the Prophet's saying, “Do not revile time, for time is God”; he gives no grading.
RAZI-FULL:v28p262/r6.anchor: قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( لا تسبوا الدهر

RAZI-FULL:v28p262/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p262/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p262/r7.claim: Temporal priority and posteriority have reality only through God; without God there would be no temporal order to revile.
RAZI-FULL:v28p262/r7.anchor: والبعدية والقبلية حقيقة لإثبات الله ولا مفهوم للزمان إلا ما به القبلية والبعدية

RAZI-FULL:v28p262#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p262#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p262#2/r1.claim: Although Arabs use الأولة as feminine of الأول, أولى looks like a comparative whose feminine should not take ة; أول is exceptional, resembling both أربع/أرنب and الأكبر/الأصغر, so أولى is also used.
RAZI-FULL:v28p262#2/r1.anchor: أول لما كان أفعل وليس له فاعل شابه الأربع والأرنب فجاز إلحاق التاء به

RAZI-FULL:v28p262#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p262#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p262#2/r2.claim: The forms الأولة and الأولى explain why أولا may appear with or without tanwin: the ة form permits it, while الأولى is diptote.
RAZI-FULL:v28p262#2/r2.anchor: فمن قال بأن تأنيث أول أولة فهو كالأربع والأربعة فجاز التنوين

RAZI-FULL:v28p262#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p262#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p262#2/r3.claim: The Qurʾanic feminine الأولى is more common, so the usual form leaves tanwin; Arabs also preserve the etymological أولة, though Rāzī calls it weaker.
RAZI-FULL:v28p262#2/r3.anchor: الأشهر ترك التنوين لأن الأشهر أن تأنيثه أولى وعليه استعمال القرآن

RAZI-FULL:v28p262#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p262#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p262#2/r4.claim: A further grammatical proposal is that أفعل is diptote only when its feminine is exclusively فعلى; allowing a ة feminine removes that restriction.
RAZI-FULL:v28p262#2/r4.anchor: منع الصرف من أفعل لا يكون إلا إذا لم يكن تأنيثه إلا فعلى

STUDYQURAN:53:25/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:25/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:25/r1.claim: Pagan followers seem to believe in a god and hereafter, but fit them to conjectures and caprices, effectively denying God’s mastery of both worlds.
STUDYQURAN:53:25/r1.anchor: by attempting to make this understanding conform to their conjectures and caprices, they in effect deny that God is the Master of this world and the next

QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r1.claim: The hereafter and this world belong to God as creator and owner; He alone has complete sovereignty, while every creature is inherently deficient.
QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r1.anchor: له الآخرة والأولى خلقا وملكا ، فهو الملك المالك صاحب الملك التام . فأما المخلوق فالنقص لازم للكل

TABATABAI:53:24-27/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:24-27/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:24-27/r4.claim: God’s exclusive ownership of this life and the next is the reason people cannot acquire their wishes simply by wishing.
TABATABAI:53:24-27/r4.anchor: تفريعه على سابقه من تفريع العلة للمعلول للدلالة على التعلق والارتباط ففيه تعليل للجملة السابقة

TABATABAI:53:24-27/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:24-27/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:24-27/r5.claim: Neither the first life nor the Hereafter has a partner with God in its dominion.
TABATABAI:53:24-27/r5.anchor: والمعنى ليس يملك الإنسان ما تمناه بمجرد التمني لأن الآخرة والأولى لله سبحانه ولا شريك له في ملكه

FARRA:v3p99/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p99/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p99/r4.claim: The afterlife and the present life, and their reward, belong to God.

THALABI:v9p147#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p147#2/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p147#2/r3.claim: Both the afterlife and this world belong to God: He gives what He wills to whom He wills and denies whom He wills.
THALABI:v9p147#2/r3.anchor: فلله الآخرة والأولى يعطي من يشاء ما يشاء، ويحرم من يشاء ما يشاء.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p49#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p49#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p49#2/r1.claim: Both the afterlife and this world belong to God; no one owns or receives anything from either without His permission, refuting what the unbeliever wishes for.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p49#2/r1.anchor: أي لا يملك فيهما ولا منهما أحد شيئا إلا بإذنه؛ لأنهما (¬2) له.

ITQAN:v3p37/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p37/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p37/r6.claim: The reversed order “Hereafter and this world” is chosen to preserve the verse ending; the same concern shapes “We gathered you and the earlier peoples.”
ITQAN:v3p37/r6.anchor: وأما قوله ﴿ فلله الآخرة والأولى ﴾ فلمراعاة الفاصلة وكذا قوله ﴿ جمعناكم والأولين ﴾

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:25-30/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:25-30/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:25-30/r1.claim: Both the Hereafter and this world belong to God, and nothing occurs in either except by His will.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:25-30/r1.anchor: فلا يجري في الدارين إلا ما يريد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p410/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p410/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p410/r2.claim: Both the afterlife and this world belong to God; no one possesses anything in them except by His permission.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p410/r2.anchor: بل لله الآخرة والأولى، لا يملك أحد فيهما شيئا إلا بإذنه
